retirement_age.notes: Mandatory retirement age in the public service is 60 (Public Service Commission rules); persons with disabilities may serve to 65. Private-sector ages depend on the scheme rules or employment contract. Kenya has no single national pension age.

political_system: presidential republic with devolved county governments

offices.office: Head of state and head of government
offices.title: President

open_questions: President's term_ends left null: his term runs until the next president is sworn in after the 2027-08-10 election (sworn-in date set by Article 141). A High Court ruling reported by The EastAfrican (2026) said the President's term is not fixed at five years and suspended its effect until after the next general election.

Median age left null: the only figure found (21.1 for 2025, PopulationPyramid.net) could not be cross-checked; a similar site disagreed with Worldometer for Nigeria, so the method is uncertain. Find the UN WPP 2024 table directly.

Population: UN/UNFPA gives 57.5 million for 2025, while a Wikipedia table lists an official projection of 54.2 million for 1 July 2026. The UN figure is used; check the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics directly.

Retirement age: figure of 60 comes from the Salaries and Remuneration Commission page on public-service pensions and a Star article citing the Public Service Commission manual. A 2026 rule for some university staff was reported (65) but not verified.
The incumbent is reported to be expected to seek a second term (People Daily, June 2026); no official candidate list exists yet.
